To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nos TTE can function in a cell-type specific manner in the nervous system to repress the expression of genes that regulate the moling cycle.
a common translational control element, the Translational Control Elements (TCE), functions in both early embryonic patterning and in the regulation of the molting cycle.
the nos TCF is a common translational control element that regulates gene expression in both early and late development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of gene expression at the level of translation.
the regulation of maternal mRNA translation during development.
the molecular basis of gene regulation during development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TCE functions as a translational repressor of the nos transcript in a number of tissues during development, including the nervous system.

TCE-mediated repression of maternal mRNAs can function in the nervous system to control neuroendocrine signaling and that the mechanisms that control maternal mRNAs may have a more general role during development.
TCE-mediated repression of nos mRNA is not only essential for anterior-posterior axis patterning, but also plays a crucial role in the regulation of the molting cycle in the DrosophILA brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single cis-acting element in a maternal mRNA can function in two separate developmental processes, axial patterning and molting.
the nos Tce is a general translational control element that functions in both the early embryo and the adult nervous system to regulate gene expression in a spatial and/or temporal manner.
the TCE is a conserved mechanism for translational repression in Drosophilla and that it is used in the nervous system to control the timing of gene expression in neuroendocrine cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same mechanism of repression that is important for patterning the early embryo is used in the nervous system to regulate the molting process.
a common translational repression mechanism that functions during early embryonic development also functions later in development in the nervous system.
the same mechanism can be used in different contexts to control different processes.
